subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In 1290 King Edward I issued an Edict expelling which community from England?
questions.explain: Edward I expelled England's Jewish population in 1290; they were not readmitted until the 1650s.

questions.q: The arrival of the ship Empire Windrush in 1948 is associated with migration from where?
questions.explain: The Windrush brought Caribbean migrants in 1948, often invited to help rebuild post-war Britain.

questions.q: The medieval Jewish community expelled in 1290 were not officially allowed to return to England until which century?
questions.explain: Jewish people were readmitted to England in the 1650s under Oliver Cromwell, in the 17th century.

questions.q: Caribbean migrants invited to Britain after 1948 were especially recruited to work in which new institution?
questions.explain: Many Windrush-era migrants were recruited to staff the new NHS and London Transport after 1948.

questions.q: The Commonwealth Immigrants Act of 1962 did what?
options: Restricted migration from the Commonwealth by introducing controls
questions.explain: The 1962 Act began restricting Commonwealth migration by requiring work vouchers.

questions.q: In the late 19th century, many Jewish migrants came to areas such as London's East End fleeing what?
options: The collapse of the Ottoman Empire
Pogroms and persecution in Eastern Europe
questions.explain: Jewish migrants fled pogroms in Russia and Eastern Europe, settling in districts like Whitechapel.

questions.q: In 1972, Britain received tens of thousands of Asian migrants expelled from which country?
questions.explain: Idi Amin expelled Uganda's Asian population in 1972, and many came to Britain.

questions.q: In which year did the Norman Conquest bring William of Normandy and his followers to power in England?
questions.explain: William of Normandy conquered England in 1066 after the Battle of Hastings.

questions.q: Why did the Normans build so many castles after 1066?
options: To control and hold down the conquered English population
questions.explain: Norman castles were tools of control, dominating the English they had conquered.

questions.q: The Norman Conquest of 1066 brought which lasting change as Norman migrants ruled England?
options: The use of French among the ruling elite and new castles
questions.explain: The Norman elite brought French language, feudal landholding and castle-building to England.

questions.q: The Vikings who settled in eastern and northern England created a region governed by Danish law known as what?
questions.explain: The Danelaw was the area of England under Scandinavian control and Danish customs.

questions.q: The Vikings first raided which famous English monastery in 793?
questions.explain: The Viking raid on the monastery of Lindisfarne in 793 marked the start of the Viking Age in Britain.

questions.q: In the 1840s, large-scale Irish migration to Britain was driven mainly by what?
questions.explain: The Irish Potato Famine of the 1840s drove huge numbers of Irish people to settle in British cities.

questions.q: In the 19th century, Irish migrants in British cities often faced which difficulties?
questions.explain: Irish migrants commonly met prejudice and crowded into poor, low-paid living conditions.

questions.q: After Britain joined the European Community/EU, a notable wave of migration came from where in the 2000s?
options: Eastern European countries such as Poland
questions.explain: After the EU expanded in 2004, many migrants came from Eastern European states such as Poland.

questions.q: The abolition of the British transatlantic slave trade was passed by Parliament in which year?
questions.explain: Parliament abolished the British slave trade in 1807; slavery itself in the empire ended in 1833.

questions.q: Many Huguenots who settled in Spitalfields in London became known for which luxury craft?
questions.explain: Huguenot refugees brought skilled silk-weaving to areas such as Spitalfields in London.

questions.q: In which year did the Empire Windrush arrive in Britain?
questions.explain: The Empire Windrush docked at Tilbury in 1948, a landmark in Commonwealth migration to Britain.

questions.q: The Aliens Act of 1905 was passed largely in response to which wave of migration?
questions.explain: The 1905 Aliens Act restricted immigration amid arrivals of Jewish migrants fleeing Eastern Europe.

questions.q: Flemish migrants who came to medieval England were especially known for which trade?
questions.explain: Flemish weavers brought valuable cloth-making skills that boosted England's textile industry.

questions.q: The British Nationality Act of 1948 did what?
options: Gave Commonwealth citizens the right to live and work in Britain
questions.explain: The 1948 Act granted Commonwealth citizens British nationality and the right to settle, encouraging migration.

questions.q: Before the 1290 expulsion, medieval Jewish communities in England were especially associated with which activity, since Christians were barred from it?
questions.explain: Jewish people were often money-lenders, as the Church forbade Christians from charging interest.
